paragraphs: The future of the Apple Vision Pro headset is reportedly in flux, with no internal agreement on the design of possible future models. In fact, a successor to the pricey mixed-reality headset might never see the light of day.
Fans have wanted a lighter, more comfortable Vision Pro since launch. But Apple is said to be weighing four very different concepts for the headset’s sequel — and a release isn’t guaranteed.

Apple launched the Vision Pro in 2024 as its first major new product category in years. The headset combines high-resolution displays, eye and hand tracking, and spatial audio to create what Apple calls “spatial computing.” But its $3,499 starting price (since upped to $3,699), along with its weight, greatly limited its appeal compared to more affordable VR headsets.

On Sunday, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman wrote that Apple is working on completely overhauling the headset. This project is code-named N224 but, in his latest Power On newsletter, Gurman says it’s on “life support” and might never ship.

As for the concepts, engineers are exploring one where the computing hardware and battery would be in a separate puck. That’s the same approach Meta took with its new VR glasses. The current Vision Pro already uses an external battery pack. But some inside Apple reportedly dislike the puck idea and want an integrated design.
The second idea involves keeping the current Vision Pro’s egg-shaped body. Apple is reportedly testing plastic, titanium and other metals to make it lighter.
The fact that there’s no agreement about even the basic layout of the product doesn’t bode well for its future.

Gurman also pointed to a management shake-up affecting Vision Pro development. Previously, the Vision team directly reported to John Ternus. But now that he’s CEO, the group sits one layer further from the top, with Johny Srouji as Apple’s chief hardware officer.
